mainTopic: An עירוב that is hard to reach: in a pit, on top of a reed, or in a locked cupboard
overview: The גמרא finishes asking where an עירוב placed in a deep pit is valid. It settles on a pit in a כרמלית, following רבי's rule that a rabbinic prohibition (שבות) does not apply during בין השמשות. A new משנה teaches that an עירוב on top of a detached reed or pole stuck in the ground is valid, even a hundred אמות high. רב אדא בר מתנא asks how the earlier clause can follow רבי while this one seems to follow the רבנן. רב חסדא accepts the split. רבינא says the whole משנה is רבי, and the reed case has its own worry that he might snap the reed off. A story about רב נחמן letting students sit on pressed-down marsh reeds on שבת leads to a distinction between hard reeds, which count as trees, and soft reeds, which count as vegetables. A last משנה rules that an עירוב locked in a cupboard with a lost key is still valid. The גמרא explains this as a cupboard of loosely stacked bricks, following רבי מאיר, and then limits it to יום טוב. That limit is challenged from רבי אליעזר's distinction between a key lost in the city and one lost in the field, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A pit inside a private domain makes the ruling obvious
steps.stepSummary: If the pit is in a רשות היחיד, the משנה's ruling is too obvious to need teaching, because a רשות היחיד extends both upward and downward without limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious! A private domain goes up to the sky. Just as it goes up, it also goes down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is testing one possible case for the earlier משנה about an עירוב in a pit, a pit inside a רשות היחיד, and rejects it as too obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A רשות היחיד has no height limit above it, and the same is true below it. A deep pit inside a private domain is therefore simply part of that same domain. The person and his עירוב are in one domain, so there is nothing new for the משנה to teach.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious, so why would the משנה need to say it?
A private domain, an enclosed area
Goes up to the sky, meaning it has no height limit

steps.confusionAlert: This amud begins in the middle of the גמרא's question. The earlier משנה said an עירוב placed in a pit is valid even if the pit is a hundred אמות deep. Here the גמרא is checking which case that ruling refers to.

phrases.aramaic: פְּשִׁיטָא! רְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד עוֹלָה עַד לָרָקִיעַ,
phrases.english: It is obvious! The private domain rises up to the sky,
phrases.notes: So the case can't be a pit inside a private domain.

phrases.english: and just as it goes up above,
so too it goes down below.
phrases.notes: So the bottom of the pit is the same domain as the area around it.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא! רְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד עוֹלָה עַד לָרָקִיעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the גמרא's question on the previous amud about what case the pit ruling describes.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the pit in the משנה is located in a רשות היחיד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the whole area is one private domain, extending downward without limit, the ruling teaches nothing new.

steps.title: Suggesting the pit is in a public domain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes instead that the pit sits in a רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the pit is located in a public domain.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the private-domain case was too obvious, the גמרא suggests a new setting, a pit in a public area. This is a setup line that prepares the next challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pit ten טפחים deep and four wide counts as a separate רשות היחיד even when it is located inside a רשות הרבים. That creates two different domains, which could make the ruling meaningful. The גמרא will now test whether this proposal actually works.

keyTerms.meaning: That it stands, or is located

phrases.english: Rather, it is a case where the pit is located in the public domain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected private-domain case with a public-domain case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The pit is inside a רשות היחיד.
steps.terutzMaskana: The pit is inside a רשות הרבים, which creates two different domains.

steps.title: Both options in a public domain fail
steps.stepSummary: If the person intends to rest above, his עירוב is in a different domain and is invalid. If he intends to rest below, the ruling is obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where did he intend to establish his שבת place? If above, he is in one place and his עירוב is in another place. If below, it is obvious, since he and his עירוב are in one place!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the public-domain suggestion. Either way the person intends to rest, the משנה's ruling does not make sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he chooses to rest above, in the רשות הרבים, his עירוב is down in the pit, which is a רשות היחיד. He could not bring it up without breaking the Torah prohibition of carrying, so the עירוב cannot work. If he chooses to rest inside the pit itself, he and his עירוב are in the same domain, and that is too obvious to teach.

keyTerms.meaning: He intended to establish his שבת resting place
Above, on the ground next to the pit
His עירוב, the food that sets his שבת place

phrases.english: Where did he intend to establish his Shabbat residence?
If above,

phrases.aramaic: הוּא בְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד וְעֵירוּבוֹ בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר הוּא.
phrases.english: then he is in one place and his עירוב is in another place.
phrases.notes: The pit is a separate private domain, so the עירוב cannot be brought up to him.

phrases.english: If below, it is obvious,
since he and his עירוב are in one place!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the public-domain case proposed in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the pit is located in a רשות הרבים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This is a dilemma. Resting above makes the עירוב invalid, and resting below makes the ruling obvious.

steps.title: The case is a pit in a כרמלית, resting above
steps.stepSummary: The ruling is needed for a pit located in a כרמלית, where the person intends to rest above the pit.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed only where the pit is in a כרמלית and he intended to rest above.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה refers to a pit located in a כרמלית, with the person choosing to rest up on the כרמלית ground. This sets up the explanation in the next step of why such an עירוב works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כרמלית is an in-between area that the חכמים treated like a public domain. Carrying from a pit, which is a רשות היחיד, into a כרמלית is forbidden only by rabbinic law, not by Torah law. That difference is what will let the עירוב be valid.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for this case
An in-between area, neither fully private nor public, whose carrying rules are rabbinic

phrases.english: It is needed only where the pit is located in a כרמלית
and he intended to establish his Shabbat residence above,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the dilemma of step 3 by choosing a third type of location.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The pit is in either a רשות היחיד or a רשות הרבים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The pit is in a כרמלית and he rests above it.

steps.title: Following רבי: no rabbinic decree at twilight
steps.stepSummary: The עירוב works because the משנה follows רבי, who holds that rabbinic prohibitions (שבות) do not apply during בין השמשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this follows רבי, who said: anything forbidden only as a שבות, they did not decree it during בין השמשות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the עירוב in the כרמלית case is valid, even though moving it from the pit to the כרמלית is normally forbidden. The answer is that this משנה follows רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירוב takes effect at בין השמשות, the twilight time when Shabbat begins. According to רבי, rabbinic prohibitions were not applied at that time. Since carrying from the pit to the כרמלית is only a שבות, at that moment he could bring the עירוב up, so the עירוב counts as reachable and is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Twilight, the moment the עירוב takes effect

steps.whatToRemember: An עירוב in a pit is valid when the pit is in a כרמלית and the person rests above it. This works because, according to רבי, the rabbinic carrying prohibition did not apply at בין השמשות.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of רבי, that there is no שבות at בין השמשות, comes up many times in the laws of עירוב, because the עירוב takes effect at exactly that moment.

phrases.english: And this follows רבי, who said:
Anything that is forbidden only because of a rabbinic decree
they did not decree it during twilight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer of step 4 by explaining why the כרמלית case gives a valid עירוב.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the משנה to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the עירוב cannot be moved from the pit to the כרמלית, it should be invalid.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי, no שבות applies at בין השמשות, so the עירוב is reachable and valid.

steps.title: New משנה: an עירוב on top of a reed or pole
steps.stepSummary: An עירוב placed on top of a detached reed or pole stuck in the ground is valid, even if it is a hundred אמות high.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he placed it on top of a reed or on top of a pole, when it is detached and stuck in the ground, even a hundred אמות high, it is an עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that an עירוב placed high up on a reed or pole is valid, as long as the reed or pole is detached and only stuck into the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the reed was cut off and then stuck in the ground, it is not a growing plant. He can pull it out and reach his עירוב. The height does not matter, even a hundred אמות.

keyTerms.meaning: Detached from the ground and then stuck back into it

steps.confusionAlert: The condition "detached and stuck" is important. Using a living, attached plant raises other problems, so the משנה specifies a reed that was cut and then stuck into the ground.

phrases.english: MISHNA: If he placed it on top of a reed
or on top of a pole,
when it is detached and stuck into the ground,
even if it is a hundred אמות high,
it is a valid עירוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה after the pit discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עירוב on top of a detached reed or pole stuck in the ground is valid, even a hundred אמות high.

steps.title: The reed case seems to follow the רבנן, but the earlier case followed רבי
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר מתנא infers from the משנה that an עירוב on an attached reed is invalid. That fits the רבנן, who apply שבות during בין השמשות. But this clashes with the claim that the previous clause follows רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: רב אדא בר מתנא raised a contradiction before רבא. The משנה says a reed that was detached and then stuck in the ground works. That implies a reed that was not detached (still growing) does not work. Whose view is this? It must be the רבנן, who say that anything forbidden as a שבות was forbidden even during בין השמשות. But didn't you say the first clause follows רבי? Can the first clause be רבי and the later clause be the רבנן?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the reed משנה, and רב אדא בר מתנא attacks it with a contradiction. The reed case seems to follow the רבנן, while the tree case before it was said to follow רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only allows a reed that was 'detached and stuck in.' That suggests a reed still growing in place is not allowed. The likely reason is that using something attached to the ground is a rabbinic prohibition (שבות), and the person could not take the עירוב down during בין השמשות. That reasoning only works for the רבנן, but step 5 said the משנה follows רבי, who holds that שבות does not apply during בין השמשות. Two neighboring clauses following opposite views is hard to accept.

keyTerms.meaning: Detached; cut off from where it grew
Twilight, the uncertain time when שבת begins

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'רבי' means רבי יהודה הנשיא, the specific תנא who says שבות does not apply during בין השמשות. It is not a general word for 'a rabbi.' 'רבנן' means the חכמים who disagree with him.

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ רָמֵי לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָא לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Adda bar Mattana raised a contradiction before Rava:
phrases.notes: רָמֵי literally means 'threw together': he set two sources against each other.

phrases.english: Detached and then stuck in the ground — yes (valid).
phrases.notes: This is the משנה's case of the reed.

phrases.english: Not detached and stuck in (still growing) — no (invalid).
phrases.notes: We learn this from the way the משנה words it.

phrases.english: Whose view is this? It is the Rabbis,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמְרִי: כׇּל דָּבָר שֶׁהוּא מִשּׁוּם שְׁבוּת
phrases.english: who say: anything that is forbidden as a rabbinic prohibition
they decreed against it even during twilight.
phrases.notes: So he could not take the עירוב off a growing reed at the key moment.

phrases.english: But didn't you say the first clause follows Rabbi!
The first clause Rabbi and the later clause the Rabbis?!

steps.triggerLanguage: רָמֵי לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָא לְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reed ruling of step 6 by setting it against the claim in step 5 that the משנה follows רבי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the previous clause (the tree case) follows רבי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reed clause implies that a growing reed is invalid. That only makes sense if שבות applies during בין השמשות, which is the view of the רבנן. So the two neighboring clauses would follow opposite תנאים.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the first clause is רבי and the later clause is the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that this same question was already asked of רב חסדא. רב חסדא accepted that the two clauses follow different תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: רמי בר חמא already raised this contradiction before רב חסדא, and he answered him: the first clause is רבי, and the later clause is the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers by quoting an earlier answer of רב חסדא. Yes, the two clauses really do follow two different תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of explaining away the contradiction, this answer simply accepts it. The tree case follows רבי, so the עירוב is valid there. The reed case follows the רבנן, so a growing reed is invalid because of שבות. A משנה can sometimes combine clauses from different תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: He answered him (literally, 'changed it for him,' resolving a difficulty)

phrases.english: He (Rava) said to him: This contradiction was already raised
by Rami bar Chama before Rav Chisda,
and he answered him:
The first clause is Rabbi, and the later clause is the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּבָר רָמֵי לֵיהּ רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא לְרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 7 by accepting the split.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the משנה between two תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed both clauses must follow one תנא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The tree clause follows רבי, and the reed clause follows the רבנן.

steps.title: רבינא: the whole משנה is רבי, with a special worry about snapping the reed
steps.stepSummary: רבינא keeps the whole משנה as רבי. The reed case is invalid for a different reason: a decree that the person might snap off the reed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: The whole משנה follows רבי. The later clause is a special decree, out of concern that he might snap it off.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a second answer. Both clauses follow רבי, and the reed case is explained by a different concern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא says the reed ruling is not about the general שבות of using a growing plant during בין השמשות. A soft growing reed is easy to break, so the Sages feared the person would snap it off to reach his עירוב. A tree does not raise this worry, so the tree case can still follow רבי with no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: All of it; the whole משנה

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to the contradiction. רב חסדא says the clauses follow different תנאים. רבינא says the whole משנה is רבי, and the reed case has its own worry that he might snap it off.

phrases.english: Ravina said: It is all Rabbi,
and the later clause is a decree lest he snap it off.
phrases.notes: This concern applies to a soft reed, not to a tree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the קשיא of step 7, avoiding the split proposed in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Giving a new reason for the later clause
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The reed is invalid because of שבות during בין השמשות, which is the view of the רבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The reed is invalid because of a separate decree that he might snap it off, so רבי can agree.

steps.title: An army in נהרדעא and רב נחמן's instruction to press down reeds
steps.stepSummary: A story: an army came to נהרדעא. רב נחמן told his students to press reeds together in the marsh so they could sit on them the next day, on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain army came to נהרדעא. רב נחמן said to them (the students): Go out and press reeds together in the marsh, and tomorrow we will go and sit on them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story connected to reeds. This is a setup: the גמרא will next examine what this story teaches about using reeds on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The army took over the study hall, so there was no room to learn. רב נחמן had the students bend and press the reeds before שבת so that on שבת they could sit on them. The question the story raises is why pressing them down in advance helps, and how this fits with the rules about using growing plants.

keyTerms.meaning: נהרדעא, a Torah center in Babylonia

phrases.english: There was a certain army that came to Nehardea.
phrases.notes: They took quarters in the study hall.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to them (the students):
Go out and press down reeds in the marsh,
and tomorrow (on Shabbat) we will go and sit on them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a practical story about using reeds on שבת. It connects to the discussion of reeds and of using growing plants.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן allowed sitting on reeds on שבת if they were pressed down before שבת.

steps.title: Challenge to רב נחמן from the משנה about reeds
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא (or רב עוקבא בר אבא) challenges רב נחמן. The משנה says a reed counts only if it was cut and then stuck into the ground. An attached reed does not count, so how could רב נחמן allow using attached reeds on שבת?
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא challenged רב נחמן (some say it was רב עוקבא בר אבא who challenged him). The משנה says: if the reed was cut off and then stuck into the ground, yes, it may be used. If it was not cut off and not stuck in, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן's instruction from Step 10, where he told his students to press reeds together and sit on them on שבת. The challenge comes from the wording of our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only approves a reed that was cut off (תלוש) and then stuck back in the ground (נעוץ). That suggests a reed still growing in the ground may not be used on שבת. רב נחמן's students were going to sit on reeds that were still attached, so his ruling seems to go against the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Detached, cut off from the ground

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא לְרַב נַחְמָן,
phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama raised an objection to Rav Naḥman,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַב עוּקְבָא בַּר אַבָּא לְרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: and some say it was Rav Ukva bar Abba who objected to Rav Naḥman:
If it was detached and then stuck in, yes;
if it was not detached and not stuck in, no.
phrases.notes: A reed still growing in the ground may not be used.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא לְרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב נחמן's practical instruction from Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's permission to sit on attached, pressed-together reeds on שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה approves only a reed that was cut and then stuck in. So an attached reed may not be used on שבת, and רב נחמן's students were using attached reeds.

steps.title: רב נחמן: the משנה is about hard reeds
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the משנה speaks about hard reeds (עוזרדין). Those count like trees, so they may not be used while attached. Soft reeds are different.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There, in the משנה, we are dealing with hard reeds.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends his ruling. He says the משנה is talking about a different kind of reed from the soft marsh reeds his students used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hard reeds (עוזרדין) are firm like trees, so using one while it is attached is like using a tree on שבת, which is forbidden. Soft reeds are treated like vegetables or grasses, which may be used. So the משנה and רב נחמן's case do not conflict.
steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is not saying the משנה is wrong. He is limiting it to one kind of reed (hard ones) and placing his own case in a different kind (soft ones).

phrases.english: He said to him: There, it is dealing with hard reeds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: the משנה deals with hard reeds, and רב נחמן deals with soft reeds
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה forbids all attached reeds.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only hard reeds (עוזרדין) are forbidden. Soft reeds may be used.

steps.title: Source for the hard/soft distinction: two ברייתות that clash
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asks how we know that hard and soft reeds are treated differently. He brings two ברייתות about כלאים in a vineyard. One calls reeds a kind of tree, and the other calls reeds a kind of vegetable, so they seem to contradict each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do you know that we distinguish between hard reeds and reeds that are not hard? As a ברייתא teaches: Reeds, boxthorn, and thistles are a kind of tree, and they are not כלאים in a vineyard. And another ברייתא teaches: Reeds, cassia, and bulrushes are a kind of vegetable, and they are כלאים in a vineyard. These contradict each other!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the proof for the hard/soft distinction. It shows two ברייתות that seem to clash. The way this clash gets solved in the next step is the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of כלאים בכרם forbids planting vegetables in a vineyard, but not trees. One ברייתא lists reeds as trees, which are allowed in a vineyard. The other lists reeds as vegetables, which are forbidden there. That is a direct contradiction about reeds.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do you say this?
Forbidden mixture of crops planted in a vineyard

phrases.english: And from where do you say

phrases.aramaic: דְּשָׁנֵי לַן בֵּין עוּזְרָדִין לְשֶׁאֵין עוּזְרָדִין —
phrases.english: that we distinguish between hard reeds and reeds that are not hard?
As it was taught: Reeds, boxthorn, and thistles
are a kind of tree,
and they are not כלאים in a vineyard.
phrases.notes: Trees planted near vines are not כלאי הכרם.

phrases.english: And another ברייתא teaches: Reeds, cassia, and bulrushes
are a kind of vegetable,
and they are כלאים in a vineyard.
They contradict each other!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְנָא תֵּימְרָא דְּשָׁנֵי לַן בֵּין עוּזְרָדִין לְשֶׁאֵין עוּזְרָדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts bringing a source to back up the distinction made in Step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That hard reeds and soft reeds have different halachic status
steps.raayaSupportSource: Two ברייתות about כלאים בכרם that classify reeds differently

steps.title: The contradiction is solved: hard reeds are trees, soft reeds are vegetables
steps.stepSummary: The only way to settle the two ברייתות is to say one speaks of hard reeds and the other of soft reeds. That proves the distinction רב נחמן relied on.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this: here it speaks of hard reeds, and there it speaks of reeds that are not hard. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction from Step 13. Settling it proves that hard and soft reeds are treated differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא that calls reeds a tree is talking about hard reeds (עוזרדין). The one that calls them a vegetable is talking about soft reeds. Since the ברייתות themselves need this distinction, רב נחמן's answer in Step 12 now has solid backing.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this; it is proven
Here... there (each source fits a different case)

steps.whatToRemember: Hard reeds (עוזרדין) count like trees, and soft reeds count like vegetables. That is why the משנה forbids using an attached reed (a hard one), while רב נחמן allowed his students to sit on soft reeds on שבת after pressing them down the day before.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from this:
here it speaks of hard reeds,
there it speaks of reeds that are not hard.
Learn from this.
phrases.notes: The גמרא confirms that the proof stands.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: כָּאן בְּעוּזְרָדִין, כָּאן בְּשֶׁאֵין עוּזְרָדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Solves the contradiction from Step 13 and finishes the proof for Step 12.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The halacha treats hard reeds and soft reeds differently, so רב נחמן's ruling stands.

steps.title: Is קידה really a vegetable? A משנה calls it a tree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the second ברייתא, which listed קידה (cassia) as a vegetable. A משנה forbids grafting rue onto white קידה because that would be grafting a vegetable onto a tree, which shows קידה is a tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is קידה a kind of vegetable?! But we learned in a משנה: One may not graft rue onto white קידה, because that is grafting a vegetable onto a tree!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a side detail in the ברייתא it just quoted. It asks how קידה can be called a vegetable when a משנה treats it as a tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא in Step 13 listed קידה as a vegetable. But the משנה in כלאים forbids grafting rue (פיגם) onto white קידה, and its reason is that this mixes a vegetable with a tree. So that משנה treats קידה as a tree, which contradicts the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Rue, an herb (treated as a vegetable)
A vegetable grafted onto a tree

phrases.english: And is cassia a kind of vegetable?!
But didn't we learn: One may not graft rue
onto white cassia,
because that is grafting a vegetable onto a tree!
phrases.notes: So white cassia must be a tree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a side challenge to a detail of the second ברייתא quoted in Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's listing of קידה as a vegetable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה treats white קידה as a tree, since grafting rue onto it counts as grafting a vegetable onto a tree.

steps.title: רב פפא: plain קידה and white קידה are different plants
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that plain קידה is a vegetable and white קידה is a tree. They are two separate plants, so there is no contradiction.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: קידה is one thing, and white קידה is another thing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא settles the side contradiction. He says the ברייתא and the משנה are talking about two different plants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא that calls קידה a vegetable means plain קידה. The משנה about grafting speaks of white קידה, which is a tree. This works the same way as the reed distinction: one name can cover two different plants with different halachic status.

keyTerms.meaning: White cassia, which is considered a tree

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Cassia is one thing, and white cassia is another thing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: קִידָּה לְחוּד, וְקִידָּה לְבָנָה לְחוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: two different plants share a similar name
steps.terutzHavaAmina: קידה is a single plant, so the ברייתא and the משנה contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Plain קידה is a vegetable, and white קידה is a tree.

steps.title: The משנה: an עירוב in a Locked Cupboard with a Lost Key
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that an עירוב locked in a cupboard is valid even if the key is lost. רבי אליעזר disagrees if the person does not know where the key is.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone put his עירוב in a cupboard and the key got lost, it is still a valid עירוב. רבי אליעזר says: if he does not know that the key is in its place, it is not a valid עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It brings a case where the עירוב is locked away and the key is lost.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier cases dealt with an עירוב that was hard to reach. Here the עירוב is safe inside the cupboard, but the person cannot open it. The תנא קמא says it still works. רבי אליעזר says it works only if the person knows the key is where it belongs.

keyTerms.meaning: Food placed before שבת so that one may walk beyond the usual limit

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If he put it in a cupboard and the key was lost
it is a valid eiruv.
Rabbi Eliezer says:
If he does not know that the key is in its place
it is not a valid eiruv.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the discussion of reeds and קידה ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עירוב locked in a cupboard with a lost key is valid. רבי אליעזר rules it invalid if the person does not know the key is in its place.

steps.title: Why Is It Valid if He Cannot Reach It?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the עירוב can be valid when the person has no way to get to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is it valid? He is in one place and his עירוב is in another place, because he cannot reach it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה. If the key is lost, the person cannot get his food, so it seems the עירוב should not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירוב works only if the person could reach and use the food at the start of שבת. A locked cupboard with no key seems to cut him off from it, so he and his עירוב are effectively in two different places.

keyTerms.meaning: And why? This often opens a challenge.

keyTerms.term: הוּא בְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד וְעֵירוּבוֹ בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר
keyTerms.meaning: He is in one place and his עירוב in another, so the עירוב cannot count

phrases.english: GEMARA: And why?
He is in one place
and his eiruv is in a different place!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי? הוּא בְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד וְעֵירוּבוֹ בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of the תנא קמא in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the עירוב is valid even though the key is lost.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An עירוב must be reachable. A locked cupboard with no key makes the food unreachable, so the עירוב should fail.

steps.title: A Brick Cupboard, Following רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל explain that the cupboard is made of bricks. The משנה follows רבי מאיר, who allows breaking an opening to take things out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and שמואל both said: here we are dealing with a cupboard made of bricks, and the משנה follows רבי מאיר. He said that one may break an opening from the start and take things out.
steps.whatsHappening: רב and שמואל answer the challenge. The person can break into the brick cupboard and reach his עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If breaking the brick wall is allowed, the food is not really locked away. The person can open a hole and take it, so the עירוב counts as reachable. This works only according to רבי מאיר's view.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start, even without a problem already existing

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel both said:
Here we are dealing with a cupboard of bricks
and it follows Rabbi Meir, who said:
One may breach from the start and take.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ הָכָא בְּמִגְדָּל שֶׁל לְבֵנִים עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the case (brick cupboard) and assigns the משנה to one תנא (רבי מאיר).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A locked cupboard with no key makes the עירוב unreachable.
steps.terutzMaskana: A brick cupboard may be broken open according to רבי מאיר, so the עירוב is reachable and valid.

steps.title: The Source for רבי מאיר's View
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a sealed house full of produce, where רבי מאיר allows breaking a hole from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: a house filled with produce that was sealed and then broke open, one may take from the place where it broke. רבי מאיר says: one may break it open from the start and take.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where רבי מאיר's view comes from. It quotes a משנה about a house full of produce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים allow taking produce only through a hole that already formed by itself. רבי מאיר allows making a new hole on purpose. That is the view רב and שמואל need for the cupboard.

keyTerms.meaning: And it broke open by itself

phrases.english: As we learned: a house that he filled with produce,
sealed, and it was breached
one may take from the place of the breach.
Rabbi Meir says:
One may breach and take from the start.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the view of רבי מאיר used in step 19.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר allows breaking an opening from the start to take things out.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a sealed house filled with produce.

steps.title: שמואל Limited That משנה to Loosely Stacked Bricks
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: שמואל himself said that the produce-house משנה speaks only about loosely stacked bricks.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב נחמן בר אדא say in the name of שמואל: that משנה is speaking about loosely stacked bricks?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer of רב and שמואל. שמואל explained elsewhere that רבי מאיר permitted breaking only a pile of bricks with no cement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Removing loose bricks is not really tearing down a building, so רבי מאיר could allow it. A normal brick cupboard is a real structure. So how can שמואל use רבי מאיר's view for a regular brick cupboard?

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say? This introduces a contradicting statement.
Layers of bricks stacked without cement

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is not against רבי מאיר. It points to a contradiction inside שמואל's own words: he limited רבי מאיר to loose bricks, yet used רבי מאיר for a brick cupboard.

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Nachman bar Adda say
that Shmuel said: it refers to layers of bricks.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר אַדָּא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the use of the produce-house משנה in steps 19-20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer of רב and שמואל that a brick cupboard may be broken open according to רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל limited רבי מאיר's ruling to loosely stacked bricks. A real brick cupboard should not be breakable, so the עירוב is still unreachable.

steps.title: Our Cupboard Is Also Loosely Stacked Bricks
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the cupboard in our משנה is also made of loosely stacked bricks.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, the cupboard is made of loosely stacked bricks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing the case even more. The cupboard is built from loose bricks with no cement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the cupboard is just stacked bricks, removing some is not breaking a real building, so רבי מאיר allows it. The person can reach his עירוב, and the משנה's ruling stands.
steps.whatToRemember: At this stage, the עירוב in the locked cupboard is valid because the cupboard is made of loosely stacked bricks. According to רבי מאיר one may take bricks out to reach the food. The next steps narrow this answer further to יום טוב (step 24) and then challenge it (step 25).

phrases.english: Here too, it is layers of bricks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the case further to fit שמואל's limitation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Our cupboard is a regular brick structure, which רבי מאיר would not allow breaking.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our cupboard is made of loosely stacked bricks, so even שמואל agrees רבי מאיר allows opening it.

steps.title: רבי זירא limits breaking open to יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proof from the produce-house משנה. רבי זירא said that breaking a hole was allowed only on יום טוב, not on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי זירא say: they allowed it only on יום טוב, but not on שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from the last steps. The produce-house משנה, which allows breaking a hole, was said only about יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The explanation of our משנה depended on the produce-house משנה, which lets you break through loose bricks. But רבי זירא says that permission is only for יום טוב. So how can we use it to explain an עירוב that might be needed for שבת, when breaking open would be forbidden?

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say (introduces a challenge from someone's known statement)

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Zeira say:
They said it regarding Yom Tov,
phrases.notes: This goes back to the משנה about the produce-house, the one that allows breaking a hole.

phrases.english: but not regarding Shabbat!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source that was used to support the loose-bricks answer in Step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using the produce-house משנה (breaking open loose bricks) to explain why the עירוב in our משנה is valid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי זירא limits the produce-house permission to יום טוב. That means breaking open would be forbidden on שבת, so the explanation cannot work for a שבת עירוב.

steps.title: Our משנה is also about יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that our משנה is also talking about an עירוב made for יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it is talking about יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts רבי זירא's limit. It answers that our cupboard case is also about יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of rejecting רבי זירא, the גמרא narrows our משנה to fit him. If the עירוב was made for יום טוב, then breaking open the loose bricks is allowed, and the עירוב is valid.

phrases.english: Here too, it is on Yom Tov.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 23 by narrowing the case of our משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) of our משנה to יום טוב
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Our משנה might apply to שבת, where breaking open is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה speaks only about an עירוב for יום טוב, where breaking open the loose bricks is allowed.

steps.title: Why would city versus field matter on Yom Tov?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the יום טוב answer. רבי אליעזר rules that a key lost in the city keeps the עירוב valid but a key lost in the field does not. On יום טוב, that difference should not matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at what is taught about this case: רבי אליעזר says, if the key was lost in the city, his עירוב is valid. If it was lost in the field, his עירוב is not valid. But if we are talking about יום טוב, what difference does it make whether it is the city or the field?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי אליעזר's ruling on our case to show that the יום טוב answer cannot be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's line between city and field makes sense only on שבת. On שבת you can bring the key through the city's joined courtyards, but you cannot carry it through a field, which is a כרמלית. On יום טוב carrying is allowed anyway, so the place where the key was lost should not matter. That suggests our משנה is about שבת after all.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (introduces a problem with the last answer)
What difference does it make to me?

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר is talking about where the KEY was lost, not where the עירוב is. The question is whether the person can carry the key back to open the cupboard.

phrases.english: If so,
this is what is taught about it:
Rabbi Eliezer says:
If it was lost in the city,
his eruv is a valid eruv;
and if it was lost in the field,
his eruv is not a valid eruv.
And if it is on Yom Tov,

phrases.aramaic: מָה לִי עִיר מָה לִי שָׂדֶה?
phrases.english: what difference is it to me whether city or field?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 24, which limited our משנה to יום טוב.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that our משנה speaks only about יום טוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר treats a key lost in the city differently from a key lost in the field. That difference only makes sense if carrying is forbidden, which is true on שבת. On יום טוב carrying is permitted, so the difference would mean nothing.
